resultados.explicacion: ¿Te importa…? is a polite way to ask a favour.
Ya voy means you are on your way right now, so I'm coming fits.
Tome is the formal command form, and a la derecha means on the right.
Cada ocho horas means every eight hours, and una pastilla is one tablet.
Me han robado means someone has stolen from me; la cartera is the wallet.
Se ha equivocado is what someone says when you dialled the wrong number.
Estar en paro is the everyday way to say you have no job.
Quedo a la espera de is a formal closing phrase for waiting for someone's answer.
Cuánto tarda asks how long it takes, and llegar means to arrive.
Nada más, gracias is the polite way to say that is everything.
Más seco means drier, and the adjective describes el paisaje, the landscape.
Se me da mal means I am bad at it, and cantar is the activity.
Me alegra verte means it makes me happy to see you.
Seguramente means probably, and llegará is the future of llegar.
Me he enterado de means I have found out or heard about something.
Me da igual means it makes no difference to me, so I don't care.
Se me cayeron las llaves means the keys fell from my hands by accident.
Se necesita is a sign asking for someone, and camarero means waiter.
Uno de cada tres means one out of every three.
Me encantaría, pero es que softens a refusal, and tengo prisa means I'm in a hurry.
No está permitido means it is not allowed, and entrar con perros means entering with dogs.
Mejor otro día literally means better another day, a polite way to postpone.
Sin querer means without meaning to, so the act was not intentional.
Ya me lo han contado means they have already told me about it.
Tiene mal carácter means someone has a bad temper, not a weak personality.
Te echo de menos means I miss you, from echar de menos.
Me torcí el tobillo means I twisted my ankle, and tobillo is the ankle.
Estar de baja means being off work on sick leave.
Para tomar aquí means to eat in, and para llevar means to take away.
El recibo de la luz is the bill for electricity, since la luz means electricity.
La vuelta is the change given back after paying, not a receipt.
Estar sin blanca is slang for having no money at all.
Suspender means to fail an exam, and Matemáticas means Maths.
Lo despidieron means they dismissed him, and ayer means yesterday.
Se me ha caducado means my passport has expired, so it is no longer valid.
Estropeada means broken or damaged, which describes the washing machine.
Estar completo means there is no room left, so the hotel is fully booked.
Se nos pinchó una rueda means one of our tyres went flat.
¿Cómo quedaron? asks how the match ended, meaning the final score.
Merece la pena means something is worth the effort or cost.
